edges.note: Pipeline stages (map/filter/reduce) take function objects/lambdas as their per-element operation.
Partial application builds the unary stage functions (e.g. filter(pred)) fed into the pipeline.
flatMap/SelectMany stages are exactly monadic bind on the list/stream monad.
A partially-applied function is realized as a closure/function object capturing the fixed arguments.

edges.cite: Wadler, 'Monads for functional programming' (1992) - Maybe monad
edges.note: Option/Maybe is the canonical monad instance: unit=Some, bind short-circuits on None.
A prism (optic; lens aka prism) focuses the present/Some case of an optional value.
A lens is a first-class, composable getter/updater pair - functions/closures over the structure.
Lens updates do copy-with-change on immutable value-typed structures rather than in-place mutation.
Relies on a closure (IIFE) capturing private state and returning the public callable/interface.
Two information-hiding techniques: JS closure-captured private state vs C forward-declared struct.
Both hide private data behind a public interface; closure encapsulation vs a private data holder object.
Both model a closed set of variants for exhaustive handling: Rust sealed trait hierarchy vs an enum/variant.
Sealing is implemented via a private empty marker supertrait unnameable outside the crate.

edges.cite: Vandevoorde & Josuttis, C++ Templates 2e - SFINAE/enable_if & detection idiom; cppreference std::enable_if
edges.note: enable_if and the detection idiom key overload viability off type-traits queries.
Competing compile-time overload-selection techniques: substitution failure vs an extra tag argument.
SFINAE predicates filter/query typelist elements when generating code over type sequences.

edges.cite: Okasaki, 'Purely Functional Data Structures' (1998), lazy evaluation
edges.note: A thunk caches (memoizes) its computed value on first force so re-forcing is O(1).
Lazy amortized persistent structures rely on memoized thunks to defer and share work.
Both stand in for a not-yet-available value: a thunk is lazy/synchronous, a future is asynchronous.
Erasure is built from an internal abstract concept + templated model - the External Polymorphism pattern.
A handle/body Bridge hides the concrete stored type behind the erased value wrapper.

edges.cite: Sean Parent, 'Inheritance Is the Base Class of Evil' (2013); Iglberger CppCon 2021
edges.note: Type erasure gives value (copyable, non-aliased) semantics to otherwise polymorphic types.
Runtime polymorphism via erased vtable vs compile-time static polymorphism via CRTP.
Typelists generate and assemble policy-based class hierarchies (e.g. GenScatterHierarchy).
Metafunctions traverse typelists to compute per-type traits and aggregate compile-time info.
A variant/tagged-union is parameterized by a typelist of its alternative types.

edges.cite: Vandevoorde & Josuttis, C++ Templates 2e - Expression Templates; Eigen MatrixBase CRTP
edges.note: Expression nodes share a static interface through a CRTP base (as in Eigen/Blaze).
Traits deduce result/element types when composing operator expression subtrees.
Both defer computation: expression templates fuse at compile time, a thunk suspends at runtime.

edges.cite: Mark Seemann on impureim sandwich vs monads
edges.note: Both separate pure logic from effects: an architectural boundary vs type-level effect sequencing.
The pure core encodes decisions and absence as returned values like Option rather than performing IO.
The thin imperative shell mirrors Humble Object: push hard-to-test IO to the edge, test the pure core.

edges.cite: Reynolds (1972) 'Definitional Interpreters'; Danvy & Nielsen 'Defunctionalization at Work' (2001)
edges.note: Replaces first-class functions with a tagged-union of occurring closures plus an apply dispatcher.
Inverse representations of closures: first-class function objects vs an enumerated tag + apply.
Continuations are passed as first-class callbacks - function objects/closures capturing the rest of the computation.
Handlers capture the delimited continuation of an effect op; a structured alternative to manual CPS.
CPS-converted calls are bounced through a trampoline to get stackless, tail-recursive execution.
Algebraic effects/handlers vs monads (and transformers) as ways to define and compose effects.
Tagless-final interpreters commonly interpret the parameterized interface into a monadic effect type.
Dimensions/units are carried as phantom type parameters absent from the runtime representation.
Encode dimensional distinctions via type-level unit parameters vs wrapping quantities in distinct newtypes.
A phantom type parameter added to a newtype wrapper tags otherwise-identical representations.
Passing/storing by copy is the systematic form of defensive copying: each holder owns an unaliased instance.
Stateful, inlinable callables vs a table of plain function pointers for indirect invocation.
